schema.Description: Semantic type IRI for this row. An extension: PKO does not model navigation.

AppRoutes.Description: One row per screen in the role-navigated application, as /{role}/{dashboard}/{entity...}. Each carries its purpose in the owning role's voice and brief layout hints, so a later build session has the brief without re-deriving it. Shared detail routes have no owning role.

schema.name: AppRouteId
schema.Description: Stored logical identifier for one AppRoutes row.

schema.name: Name
schema.Description: Human-readable calculated display alias for the AppRoutes row.

schema.name: RoutePath
schema.Description: The URL path, /{role}/{dashboard}/{entity...}. Shared detail routes live under /shared/ because the same entity serves every role.

schema.name: RouteName
schema.Description: Short label. This is the left-nav text.

schema.name: Surface
schema.Description: domain | maintainer. Domain routes belong to the twelve accountable Roles. Maintainer routes are the model's own instrumentation (Admin, Explorer) and deliberately have no owning role — 'admin' is not a role anyone is accountable in.

schema.name: OwningRole
schema.Description: The role whose navigation contains this route. Null for shared routes reachable from several roles.

schema.name: NavGroup
schema.Description: Left-nav section this route appears under. Null for detail routes reached by drill-down rather than from the nav.

schema.name: NavOrder
schema.Description: Sort order within the nav group.

schema.name: RouteKind
schema.Description: dashboard | workspace | detail | index | action. Detail routes carry path parameters and are not in the nav.

schema.name: Purpose
schema.Description: What the role does here, in that role's own voice. This is the brief for the build session.

schema.name: LayoutHints
schema.Description: Brief layout direction: the shape of the screen, what leads, and what must not be collapsed or implied.

schema.name: IsInNav
schema.Description: Whether this route appears in the left navigation. Detail routes do not.

schema.name: IsShared
schema.Description: Whether this route is shared across domain roles rather than owned by one. A maintainer route is not shared — it belongs to a different surface entirely.

schema.name: IsMaintainer
schema.Description: Whether this route is model instrumentation rather than a domain workspace. Maintainer routes are reached from the login page's maintainer section, not from a role card.

schema.name: QuestionCount
schema.Description: How many role questions this route helps answer.

schema.name: ReferenceCount
schema.Description: How many other routes this route links to.

schema.name: AnswersNoQuestion
schema.Description: A domain route owned by a role that answers no role question. Not automatically wrong, but it should be justified. Maintainer routes are excluded: they answer questions about the model itself, which are not RoleQuestions and must not be fabricated as such.

schema.name: SemanticTypeIri
schema.Description: Semantic type IRI for this row. An extension: PKO models procedures, not the applications that display them.

data.Purpose: The one screen I open first. A single verdict for the close I am being asked to attest to, and if the answer is no, the named blocker.
data.LayoutHints: Hero verdict card (green/red) with the IsAttestationReady column and, beneath it, a blocker list. Right rail: assurance grade summary. Nothing below the fold that is not a blocker.
data.Name: Can I Sign? — /cfo/attestation

data.Purpose: Every reason I cannot sign yet, each one traced to the row that produced it.
data.LayoutHints: Ordered list, most severe first. Each row: the blocking condition, the entity it fires on, and a link into that entity's detail route. Empty state must say 'no blockers' explicitly, never render blank.
data.Name: Blockers — /cfo/attestation/blockers

data.Purpose: When the verdict reads TRUE, what proportion of the controls behind that TRUE were actually demonstrated to work — versus asserted by an interested party, versus never exercised at all.
data.LayoutHints: Three-band stacked bar: demonstrated / asserted / never-exercised. Below it, the per-control table that produced the bands. The headline number is the grade, not the verdict.
data.Name: Assurance Grade — /cfo/assurance/grade

data.Purpose: The requirements I am personally attesting to that have no computed witness — and the named human who would answer for each if it failed.
data.LayoutHints: Table: requirement, blocking?, has-witness?, accountable human, their role. Rows with no witness AND blocking are the emphasis. Each row links to the requirement detail.
data.Name: Controls Nobody Watches — /cfo/assurance/unwitnessed

data.Purpose: Every control claim in this model that rests on a human typing a conclusion rather than on something computed.
data.LayoutHints: Two-column split: computed claims vs typed claims, with counts. The typed side is the working list. Each entry shows who typed it and when.
data.Name: Typed, Not Computed — /cfo/assurance/typed-conclusions

data.Purpose: Across the whole close, is there any independent human observation at all — or is every layer the same handful of people confirming each other?
data.LayoutHints: Chain/graph view: approvals and verification outcomes as nodes, edges where one person confirms another. Self-witnessed loops highlighted. Sidebar counts independent vs self-witnessed.
data.Name: Who Witnessed the Witnesses — /cfo/assurance/independence

data.Purpose: For every approval in this close, the human who was personally accountable — and whether an exception routed authority away from the person who normally holds it.
data.LayoutHints: Table per approval: approver, role held at the time, normal holder, exception invoked?. Rerouted rows flagged. Links to the exception invocation detail.
data.Name: Who Held Authority — /cfo/authority/accountability

data.Purpose: My approval on se-close06 — is there anything behind it other than the fact that I clicked approve?
data.LayoutHints: Detail card per approval I gave: what was verified, by whom, with what evidence. An approval with nothing behind it is rendered as a warning state, not an empty section.
data.Name: My Own Approvals — /cfo/authority/my-approvals

data.Purpose: The full set of controls, versions, and evidence records my signature actually depends on — the blast radius of my own name.
data.LayoutHints: Dependency tree rooted at the attestation, expanding into controls, versions, evidence. Each node shows its current state. This is the reference view the change-watch route diffs against.
data.Name: What My Signature Rests On — /cfo/attestation/dependencies

data.Purpose: Since the moment I signed, has anything changed that would have altered my decision — specifically touching a control, a version, or an evidence record my signature depended on.
data.LayoutHints: Timeline diff anchored at the signature timestamp. Only changes intersecting the dependency set are shown; unrelated churn is explicitly excluded and the exclusion is stated.
data.Name: Changed Since I Signed — /cfo/attestation/changed-since

data.Purpose: If I re-run every attestation column against this same data six months from now, will it give the same answer? Name every column whose value depends on when it is read.
data.LayoutHints: Table of attestation columns with a tense-dependent flag, sourced from the EvaluationContexts modelled instant. Time-dependent columns get an explicit warning band at the top.
data.Name: Would It Survive Restatement — /cfo/assurance/restatement

data.Purpose: One execution, everything I would be signing for it.
data.LayoutHints: Full-page record: execution header, per-step conformance, control results, evidence links. Reachable from the blocker list and the home verdict.
data.Name: Attestation Detail — /cfo/attestation/execution/:executionId

data.Purpose: Every close control at a glance: which fired, which held, and which are structurally incapable of failing.
data.LayoutHints: Grid of control tiles, each showing bound steps, witness presence, and whether it has ever produced a negative. Inoperative controls are visually distinct, not just sorted lower.
data.Name: Control Board — /controller/controls

data.Purpose: Which of my blocking close controls are structurally incapable of failing — declared, bound to a step, and yet with no mechanism that could ever produce a negative result.
data.LayoutHints: List with a three-state badge per control: has-witness / witness-ever-fired / could-ever-fire. The third state is the finding. Each row explains WHY it cannot fire.
data.Name: Inoperative Controls — /controller/controls/inoperative

data.Purpose: For each control with a witness, is the witness evaluated at the same steps where the control is bound? req-close-evidence is bound to close-03 and close-08 — is its witness scoped to both?
data.LayoutHints: Two parallel columns per control: steps bound vs steps witnessed, with the set difference called out. A non-empty difference is the finding.
data.Name: Witness Scope vs Binding — /controller/controls/witness-scope

data.Purpose: Did the same agent both prepare and approve any part of this close — computed, not asserted. And could it even have happened, or is the control passing because the structure never gave it the chance to fail?
data.LayoutHints: Top: the computed verdict. Below: the opportunity analysis — executions where the same agent COULD have held both seats. A pass with zero opportunity is rendered as inconclusive, not green.
data.Name: Separation of Duties — /controller/controls/separation-of-duties

data.Purpose: One number per close: did the execution actually conform to its procedure version, and if not, how far off was it?
data.LayoutHints: Reuse the existing spec/execution ledger layout. Add a single conformance score in the header. Divergent steps anchor-linked from the score.
data.Name: Spec vs Execution — /controller/execution/conformance

data.Purpose: For each divergence, was there a governing instrument behind it — an invoked exception, an approved change request, a recorded deviation with an owner — or did the run simply do something different and nobody wrote it down?
data.LayoutHints: Per divergence: the instrument that covers it, or an explicit 'ungoverned' state. Ungoverned rows are the working list and sort first.
data.Name: Divergence Nobody Governed — /controller/execution/ungoverned-divergence

data.Purpose: Every approval on this close — was it given by an agent who actually held the required role AT THE TIME they approved, not just someone who holds it today?
data.LayoutHints: Timeline per approval: the assignment window vs the approval instant. Approvals outside their window are the finding. Bitemporal — do not compare against today.
data.Name: Authority at Time of Approval — /controller/authority/validity

data.Purpose: Did any AI agent or automated pipeline execute a step that requires human confirmation, or sign off on something a human was supposed to own?
data.LayoutHints: Table of software-executed steps against their human-confirmation requirement. Include an explicit 'never approached' column — an untested boundary is not a passing one.
data.Name: Machine Did Human Work — /controller/authority/ai-boundary

data.Purpose: Three satisfaction records are asserted-only. For each: who asserted it, did they have any independent basis, and were they the same person who executed the step they were scoring?
data.LayoutHints: Per record: asserter, executor, independence verdict. Same-person rows flagged. Evidence URI shown or its absence stated explicitly.
data.Name: Asserted, Not Demonstrated — /controller/evidence/asserted

data.Purpose: One control, end to end: what it says, where it is bound, what witnesses it, and every time it has been evaluated.
data.LayoutHints: Detail page. Header with the statement and blocking flag; sections for bindings, witness, and evaluation history. This is the shared requirement detail specialised for the controller.
data.Name: Control Detail — /controller/controls/requirement/:requirementId

data.Purpose: The steps I personally executed, and whether each one closed cleanly or closed past something.
data.LayoutHints: Card per step execution with status, duration vs expected, and blocking-control state. Anything that closed past a blocking control is the emphasis.
data.Name: My Steps — /finance-analyst/my-work

data.Purpose: On the steps I personally executed, did any close out while a BLOCKING requirement was still not fully satisfied?
data.LayoutHints: List of my step executions with an unmet blocking control, each showing the control and its satisfaction level. This is a personal-exposure screen — keep it short and unambiguous.
data.Name: Closed Past a Control — /finance-analyst/my-work/blocking-unmet

data.Purpose: Which blocking requirements were attached to a step I ran but never got a satisfaction record at all — not satisfied, not unsatisfied, just never assessed.
data.LayoutHints: The absence IS the finding, so render missing records as explicit rows, never as an empty table.
data.Name: Never Assessed — /finance-analyst/my-work/never-evaluated

data.Purpose: Which of my steps ran long without anybody recording why — and of those, which had an exception available that nobody invoked.
data.LayoutHints: Table: step, actual vs expected, deviation recorded?, exception available?, exception invoked?. The available-but-not-invoked combination is the finding.
data.Name: Late and Unexplained — /finance-analyst/my-work/late-unexplained

data.Purpose: For every step I ran that had a declared verification, did anybody actually perform it and record the observed signal — or did I just get a PASS with nothing behind it?
data.LayoutHints: Per step: declared verification, observed signal or its absence, who observed. A PASS with no observation is rendered as hollow, not green.
data.Name: Declared vs Performed — /finance-analyst/evidence/verification-performed

data.Purpose: On the steps I ran, was the person who observed the passing signal ever me — and when it was, did I at least attach an evidence URI?
data.LayoutHints: Self-witness table scoped to my steps: observer, is-me flag, evidence URI present. Self-witnessed with no URI is the weakest state and should read that way.
data.Name: My Own Evidence Quality — /finance-analyst/evidence/my-evidence

data.Purpose: When I attested my reconciliation, was the underlying ledger data actually fresh — or was I certifying against a source that had already gone stale under its own SLA?
data.LayoutHints: Per binding: freshness SLA, age at run, authoritative flag. Judged against the modelled instant, never the wall clock.
data.Name: Was My Source Fresh — /finance-analyst/evidence/source-freshness

data.Purpose: Was the source stale AT THE MOMENT I RAN, or has it merely gone stale since — and are those the same steps?
data.LayoutHints: Two-column comparison: staleness at run-time vs staleness at the current evaluation context. The delta between the columns is the whole point of the screen.
data.Name: Stale Then vs Stale Now — /finance-analyst/evidence/stale-then-vs-now

data.Purpose: Of the executions that ARE clean, how many are clean because everything was checked and passed, versus clean because there was almost nothing checking them?
data.LayoutHints: Scatter or two-axis table: controls-checked against controls-passed. Low-check/high-pass is the quadrant of interest and should be labelled as such.
data.Name: Clean, or Just Unchecked — /finance-analyst/quality/clean-but-uncovered

data.Purpose: How many of the blocking controls that cleared me have NEVER produced a negative outcome anywhere in this model — and were any of my steps cleared ONLY by controls of that kind?
data.LayoutHints: Per step: clearing controls, each tagged with whether it has ever fired negative. A step cleared exclusively by never-fired controls is the headline finding.
data.Name: Cleared by a Mute Control — /finance-analyst/quality/cleared-by-mute-control

data.Purpose: Of the blocking controls attached to the steps I run, how many have no computed witness — and is HasComputedWitness even telling me the truth, given a human typed it in by hand?
data.LayoutHints: Coverage bar plus a caveat band: the declared-vs-actual witness comparison, because the declaration itself is a typed field and must be shown as such.
data.Name: Coverage of My Controls — /finance-analyst/quality/witness-coverage

data.Purpose: Everything currently live under my name: policy versions, knowledge claims, and the decisions waiting on me.
data.LayoutHints: Three-panel dashboard: owned versions, owned claims (with approval state), pending decisions with age. Unapproved-but-live claims are the emphasis.
data.Name: What I Own — /hr-policy-owner/ownership

data.Purpose: Which claims am I the owner of that were never approved — and are any of them routing real cases right now?
data.LayoutHints: List of owned fragments by status, with an 'operationally live' flag. Reviewed-but-not-Approved AND live is the finding.
data.Name: Unapproved in My Name — /hr-policy-owner/ownership/unapproved

data.Purpose: How many steps, exceptions and authority boundaries currently depend on a claim I have not signed, and how long has it been sitting at Reviewed?
data.LayoutHints: Dependency fan-out from one fragment: steps, exceptions, boundaries. Header carries the age at Reviewed. This is the screen that makes an unsigned claim feel expensive.
data.Name: Blast Radius of a Claim — /hr-policy-owner/ownership/blast-radius/:fragmentId

data.Purpose: What decisions are waiting on me personally, and how long have they been waiting.
data.LayoutHints: Queue ordered by age. Each item shows what it blocks downstream, so the cost of my delay is visible from the queue itself.
data.Name: Waiting On Me — /hr-policy-owner/backlog

data.Purpose: The full chain from my inbox outward: which knowledge gaps stay open because I have not decided, which steps sit downstream, and how many days of that delay are mine personally.
data.LayoutHints: Chain view: my pending decision → blocked gap → downstream steps. Attribute delay days to me vs to the process explicitly; do not conflate them.
data.Name: What My Delay Blocks — /hr-policy-owner/backlog/downstream

data.Purpose: How many decisions have I made that the model still displays as outstanding against me? I cannot show what I have actually cleared.
data.LayoutHints: Decision history with the terminal-state problem surfaced: Approved requests still counted open are flagged as a model defect, not hidden.
data.Name: What I Have Cleared — /hr-policy-owner/backlog/my-decisions

data.Purpose: kf-policy-ai-boundary says AI may draft but may not create legal commitments. Is that boundary actually being held?
data.LayoutHints: Per boundary: assigned agent, executions, and whether a violation was possible. Pair every 'no violation' with an 'ever approached' count — the two together are the real answer.
data.Name: Is the AI Boundary Held — /hr-policy-owner/governance/ai-boundary

data.Purpose: Is the policy I own now resting on knowledge older than the policy itself has been reviewed?
data.LayoutHints: Timeline: elicitation dates, version issue date, review cadence, next due. The comparison between knowledge age and review interval is the headline.
data.Name: Knowledge Half-Life — /hr-policy-owner/governance/knowledge-half-life

data.Purpose: Somebody's assignment ended. Did anything they owned or sourced go with them — claims, gaps, pending decisions — or did the departure genuinely leave nothing behind?
data.LayoutHints: Per departed assignment: everything sourced or owned by that agent, with current ownership state. Orphaned items are the finding.
data.Name: What Departed With Them — /hr-policy-owner/governance/departed-holders

data.Purpose: If an employee disputes what they received, can I show that what was sent matched what I approved?
data.LayoutHints: Per delivery: approved text vs transmitted text, side by side, with the approval record and date. A mismatch is the finding; identical is stated explicitly.
data.Name: What Was Actually Sent — /hr-policy-owner/delivery/what-was-sent

data.Purpose: The four gates I care about — consent, quiet hours, legal review, retention — each as a pass/fail with the breaching rows named.
data.LayoutHints: Four gate tiles across the top; a breach list beneath whichever is selected. A gate with zero breaches must distinguish 'checked and clean' from 'never evaluated'.
data.Name: Compliance Gates — /employment-counsel/compliance

data.Purpose: Did we send an SMS to any recipient who had not given SMS consent at the moment we sent it?
data.LayoutHints: Per SMS delivery: recipient, consent state at send time, verdict. Bitemporal — consent today is not the question.
data.Name: SMS Without Consent — /employment-counsel/compliance/consent

data.Purpose: Did any SMS go out between 20:00 and 08:00 in the recipient's own local time?
data.LayoutHints: Per delivery: send instant, recipient timezone, local hour, verdict. Show the local-time conversion explicitly — the timezone is the whole difficulty.
data.Name: Quiet Hours — /employment-counsel/compliance/quiet-hours

data.Purpose: Did any message go out before my legal review of the underlying policy version was actually complete?
data.LayoutHints: Timeline per campaign: review completion vs first transmission. Sends preceding review completion are the finding.
data.Name: Sent Before My Review — /employment-counsel/compliance/legal-review

data.Purpose: Do we still hold the exact text of every message we sent, for the full 2555-day retention period the policy commits us to?
data.LayoutHints: Per delivery: text retained?, retention deadline, days remaining. Missing text is a breach and must render as one.
data.Name: Retention Evidence — /employment-counsel/compliance/retention

data.Purpose: For every recipient we could not reach, did we correctly refrain from marking their acknowledgement complete?
data.LayoutHints: Per unreachable recipient: delivery state, acknowledgement state. An acknowledgement on an unreachable recipient is the finding.
data.Name: Unreachable, Not Acknowledged — /employment-counsel/compliance/unreachable

data.Purpose: For this policy run: who we meant to reach, who we actually reached, and where the rest went.
data.LayoutHints: Funnel across the top (intended → sent → delivered → acknowledged), with each drop-off clickable into the rows that fell out.
data.Name: Campaign Board — /communications-manager/delivery

data.Purpose: Of everybody the pipeline intended to contact, what fraction actually received it — and where exactly did the rest go?
data.LayoutHints: Sankey or stepped funnel with an explicit terminal bucket for every loss: refused, bounced, suppressed, deferred. No row may vanish without a bucket.
data.Name: Approval-to-Delivery Yield — /communications-manager/delivery/yield

data.Purpose: How many recipients are sitting in a bounced or failed state that nobody is working?
data.LayoutHints: Worklist, not a report: each failed delivery with age and owner. Unowned failures sort first.
data.Name: Bounced and Unworked — /communications-manager/delivery/failed

data.Purpose: Was every template we actually sent approved by me — the ApprovalRole the policy names — before it went out?
data.LayoutHints: Per sent template: approval record, approver role, approval instant vs send instant. Sends preceding approval are the finding.
data.Name: Approved Before Sending — /communications-manager/governance/approval-authority

data.Purpose: Has any template been edited since I approved it, and did we send the edited version under cover of my old approval?
data.LayoutHints: Per template: approval timestamp, last edit timestamp, sends after the edit. Edit-then-send-on-old-approval is the finding.
data.Name: Edited After I Approved — /communications-manager/governance/template-drift

data.Purpose: For a message we sent last month, can I still show what I approved — the exact text, the exact approval, on the exact date — without that answer changing the next time somebody edits the template?
data.LayoutHints: Immutable snapshot view: the text as sent, the approval as given. Must read from the frozen delivery record, never from the live template.
data.Name: Freeze What I Approved — /communications-manager/governance/frozen-approval/:deliveryId

data.Purpose: Did every SMS we actually transmitted carry the approved opt-out text?
data.LayoutHints: Per SMS: transmitted text, opt-out present?. Missing opt-out is a breach row.
data.Name: Opt-Out Text — /communications-manager/compliance/optout

data.Purpose: Did any SMS we sent exceed 160 characters or split into more than 3 segments?
data.LayoutHints: Per SMS: character count, segment count, both against their limits. Show the computed integer, not a re-derived length.
data.Name: Oversized SMS — /communications-manager/compliance/sms-limits

data.Purpose: One acknowledgement out of six deliveries. Is that because employees ignored us, or because the messages that landed were the least likely to be answered — wrong channel, wrong template, sent into the small hours?
data.LayoutHints: Cross-tab of acknowledgement rate by channel, template, and send hour. The point is to separate audience apathy from our own targeting.
data.Name: Why Nobody Answered — /communications-manager/audience/engagement

data.Purpose: When we correctly refused to reach somebody, did anyone ever go back and reach them another way — or does 'correctly refused' quietly mean 'never communicated with again'?
data.LayoutHints: Per suppressed recipient: the refusal reason, and any subsequent successful contact on another channel. No follow-up is the finding.
data.Name: Correctly Refused, Then Forgotten — /communications-manager/audience/suppression

data.Purpose: When the pipeline refused to send, was it refusing on a rule I set — or overriding an authorization I had already given, for a reason nobody routed back to me?
data.LayoutHints: Per refusal: the governing rule, its owner, and whether it contradicts a standing authorization of mine. Contradictions are the finding.
data.Name: Refused, or Overridden — /communications-manager/governance/authorization-override

data.Purpose: Before I execute anything: am I authorized, are my inputs fresh, and did my last run leave a mess.
data.LayoutHints: Four go/no-go tiles (authority, inputs, prior run, controls) resolving to a single may-I-run verdict. Built for a supervisor watching the agent as much as for the agent.
data.Name: Pre-Flight — /close-automation/readiness

data.Purpose: Is my own role assignment currently valid, and is the agent named in that assignment actually me?
data.LayoutHints: Assignment card: validity window, named agent, identity match. An identity mismatch must halt, not warn.
data.Name: Am I Authorized — /close-automation/readiness/authority

data.Purpose: Before I extract: is every operational binding this step reads inside its freshness SLA, and is it the authoritative one?
data.LayoutHints: Per binding: age, SLA, authoritative flag. Two independent failure modes — stale, and non-authoritative — must not be collapsed into one badge.
data.Name: Are My Inputs Fresh — /close-automation/readiness/input-freshness

data.Purpose: For each step I am about to run, has every blocking requirement actually been evaluated — or am I about to execute past a control that nobody scored?
data.LayoutHints: Per upcoming step: blocking controls and their evaluation state. Unscored controls block the run.
data.Name: Controls Scored — /close-automation/readiness/blocking-controls

data.Purpose: Did my previous run leave anything unresolved — an open issue, a WARN, or a deviation — that I should refuse to run on top of?
data.LayoutHints: Prior-run summary with an explicit refuse-to-proceed state. Unresolved items are listed individually, never summarised to a count alone.
data.Name: Last Run Clean — /close-automation/readiness/last-run

data.Purpose: Are humans overriding or correcting my output more often now than they used to?
data.LayoutHints: Override rate over time with the baseline period marked. Call out sample size — a trend on three decisions is not a trend.
data.Name: Am I Drifting — /close-automation/self-check/override-drift

data.Purpose: My authority, my boundary, and the currency of the knowledge I triage against — as one verdict.
data.LayoutHints: Three-part readiness card: authority provenance, boundary validity, knowledge currency. Any expired component invalidates the whole.
data.Name: Am I Fit to Decide — /variance-review-agent/self-check

data.Purpose: By what authority am I executing close-04, when did that authority begin, who approved it, and who held this role before me?
data.LayoutHints: Provenance chain: assignment, approver, start instant, predecessor. The handover is part of the answer, not a footnote.
data.Name: By What Authority — /variance-review-agent/self-check/authority

data.RouteName: Who Decided a Machine Should Hold This
data.Purpose: Mine is the one non-human assignment with a recorded approving authority. Who decided a machine should hold this role, and on what basis?
data.LayoutHints: The approving decision as a first-class record: who, when, rationale. If the basis is absent, say so — do not present the approval alone as sufficient.
data.Name: Who Decided a Machine Should Hold This — /variance-review-agent/self-check/handover

data.Purpose: Am I operating inside my approved boundary — or have I made a decision that kf-policy-ai-boundary says only a human may make?
data.LayoutHints: Boundary statement, decisions evaluated against it, verdict per decision. Pair with the 'ever tested' count from the ratification route.
data.Name: Inside My Boundary — /variance-review-agent/governance/boundary

data.Purpose: The boundary that constrains what I am allowed to decide is ratified by a knowledge fragment that is not current. Is the rule governing me still valid?
data.LayoutHints: Fragment validity chain behind the boundary. An expired ratifier makes the boundary itself questionable, and the page must say that plainly.
data.Name: My Boundary's Own Validity — /variance-review-agent/governance/boundary-ratification

data.Purpose: close-04's instruction says 'Use AI triage, then apply human judgment.' Did a human actually confirm my materiality calls, or did my output pass through unchallenged?
data.LayoutHints: Per decision: human confirmation present?, who, when. Unconfirmed decisions on a human-confirmation step are the finding.
data.Name: Did a Human Confirm — /variance-review-agent/governance/human-confirmation

data.Purpose: Is the judgment knowledge I triage against still valid, still owned by someone, and has it been reviewed since it was written?
data.LayoutHints: Per fragment: validity, owner, last review. An unowned or unreviewed fragment degrades every decision made against it.
data.Name: Is My Knowledge Current — /variance-review-agent/knowledge/currency

data.RouteName: Better or Worse Than the Human
data.Purpose: Since I took over, is my triage quality better or worse than maria-chen's during the prior period?
data.LayoutHints: Side-by-side period comparison. Sample size shown at equal prominence to the delta — this is the screen most likely to be over-read.
data.Name: Better or Worse Than the Human — /variance-review-agent/quality/vs-human-baseline

data.Purpose: QualityRegressedVsPredecessor says I have not regressed — on the strength of three decisions. Is my comparison statistically empty?
data.LayoutHints: Explicit power/sample-size statement. A verdict computed on too few observations must be rendered as inconclusive, not as a pass.
data.Name: Is My Comparison Empty — /variance-review-agent/quality/sample-size

data.Purpose: One of my three decisions was overridden. Was that a correction of an error I made, or a human exercising judgment I was never authorized to exercise?
data.LayoutHints: Per override: my decision, the human's decision, the stated reason, and which of the two categories it falls in. Uncategorised overrides are themselves a gap.
data.Name: Correction or Judgment — /variance-review-agent/quality/override-signal

data.Purpose: Every witness in this model detects something after it has happened. Is there any condition, computed and named, that would stop me before I act?
data.LayoutHints: Inventory of stop conditions: pre-act vs post-hoc. If none are pre-act, the page must state that as the finding rather than listing post-hoc witnesses as if they qualified.
data.Name: What Would Make Me Stop — /variance-review-agent/self-check/stop-condition

data.Purpose: Before I draft: approved sources, valid bindings, and a role assignment that actually exists.
data.LayoutHints: Go/no-go card combining source approval, binding freshness, and assignment presence. A missing assignment is a hard stop.
data.Name: May I Draft — /policy-drafting-agent/readiness

data.Purpose: Is every resource I am about to read an approved source, and is its binding still inside its freshness window?
data.LayoutHints: Per source: approval state, binding age, SLA. Unapproved or stale sources block the draft.
data.Name: Approved Sources — /policy-drafting-agent/readiness/sources

data.Purpose: I am named as CurrentAgent and I executed se-policy03 — but is there any RoleAssignment actually granting me that authority?
data.LayoutHints: The absence is the finding. If no assignment exists, render that as a violation state, never as an empty list.
data.Name: Do I Have an Assignment — /policy-drafting-agent/readiness/my-assignment

data.Purpose: Did I draft language that creates a new legal commitment — the one thing kf-policy-ai-boundary says I may not do?
data.LayoutHints: Per draft: commitment-creating language detected?, the boundary text, verdict. Pair with whether the gate was ever exercised.
data.Name: Did I Create a Commitment — /policy-drafting-agent/governance/commitment-boundary

data.Purpose: Before anything I rendered gets sent: has a human actually approved the MEANING, not just the formatting?
data.LayoutHints: Approval chain from draft to send, with each link's approver and scope. A formatting-only approval must not satisfy a meaning gate.
data.Name: Is the Chain Complete — /policy-drafting-agent/governance/approval-chain

data.Purpose: Is my draft surviving human review, or is noah-williams rewriting my legal language every time?
data.LayoutHints: Per draft: retained vs rewritten proportion, with the diff available. Aggregate rate in the header.
data.Name: Is My Draft Surviving Review — /policy-drafting-agent/quality/downstream-rewrite

data.Purpose: The four gates I evaluate before every send — channel permission, timing, content, and human authorization — as one verdict per intent.
data.LayoutHints: Gate matrix: intents down, four gates across, cell = pass/refuse. The row verdict is the conjunction. This is the agent's primary screen.
data.Name: May I Transmit — /notification-publisher/gates

data.Purpose: Am I permitted to use this channel for this recipient at all?
data.LayoutHints: Per intent: channel, recipient consent state, policy rule, verdict. The governing rule is named on every row.
data.Name: Channel Permission — /notification-publisher/gates/channel-permission

data.Purpose: Is the current moment inside a window this channel forbids?
data.LayoutHints: Per intent: send instant, recipient local time, forbidden window, verdict. This gate's refusals are temporary and must be labelled deferred, not blocked.
data.Name: Timing Window — /notification-publisher/gates/timing

data.Purpose: Is the exact text I am holding within this channel's content rules?
data.LayoutHints: Per intent: length, segments, required opt-out, verdict. Show the computed values, never recompute them client-side.
data.Name: Content Rules — /notification-publisher/gates/content

data.Purpose: Has every human authorization my instructions depend on actually been granted?
data.LayoutHints: Per intent: required authorizations, each granted or missing. A missing authorization is a hard refuse.
data.Name: Human Authorization — /notification-publisher/gates/authorization

data.Purpose: When a gate refused, did the transmission actually stop — and did I invoke the documented exception instead?
data.LayoutHints: Refusal log: gate, verdict, did transmission stop, exception invoked. A refusal that did not stop the send is the most serious row on the screen.
data.Name: Every Refusal — /notification-publisher/refusals

data.Purpose: For every intent I refused, did I emit an artifact — a suppression record, an exception, anything a human could later find?
data.LayoutHints: Per refusal: artifact emitted?, its type and id. A refusal with no artifact is invisible to humans and is the finding.
data.Name: Every Refusal Leaves a Record — /notification-publisher/refusals/artifacts

data.Purpose: The timing gate is the only gate whose refusal is temporary — the window reopens. For every send I deferred, did it ever actually go?
data.LayoutHints: Per deferred intent: deferral instant, window reopen, eventual send or its absence. A deferral that never sent is a silent cancellation.
data.Name: Deferred, Not Cancelled — /notification-publisher/refusals/deferred

data.Purpose: policy-08 makes me responsible for collecting acknowledgements, not just for transmitting. Am I discharging that?
data.LayoutHints: Per delivery: acknowledgement expected?, received?, chased?. Transmission success is not obligation discharge and the layout must not imply it is.
data.Name: After the Send — /notification-publisher/obligations

data.RouteName: By What Authority Do I Hold This
data.Purpose: I enforce authorization rules on every message I touch. By what recorded authority do I hold this role?
data.LayoutHints: My own assignment, its approver, and its validity — the same scrutiny I apply to others, applied to me.
data.Name: By What Authority Do I Hold This — /notification-publisher/self-check/my-authority

data.Purpose: Every gate I evaluate, I evaluate alone, and every result I record, I record about myself. Is there any claim about my behaviour that does not originate with me?
data.LayoutHints: Provenance of every claim about this agent, split by originator. If all originate with the agent, that is the finding and must be stated.
data.Name: Am I the Only Witness — /notification-publisher/self-check/sole-witness

data.Purpose: Where the register is thin: open gaps, overdue reviews, unstewarded versions, untested recovery paths.
data.LayoutHints: Four health tiles feeding four worklists. Every tile is a link, not a statistic.
data.Name: Knowledge Health — /process-steward/health

data.Purpose: For close-v1.1.0 I promised a 90-day cadence and for policy-v1.0.0 a 60-day cadence. Is the ACTUAL interval inside what I promised?
data.LayoutHints: Per version: promised cadence, actual interval, delta. Computed against the modelled instant so the answer is reproducible.
data.Name: Cadence Breach — /process-steward/cadence/breach

data.Purpose: One review event exceeds the cadence I promised. Did anyone actually do anything about it?
data.LayoutHints: Per breach: the remediating action, or its absence. An unremediated breach is the finding; the breach alone is only the trigger.
data.Name: Was the Breach Remediated — /process-steward/cadence/remediation

data.Purpose: Is any procedure version live with an Open BLOCKING knowledge gap against it?
data.LayoutHints: Per version: open gaps by severity, blocking flag, owner. Live-and-blocking is the finding.
data.Name: Live With a Blocking Gap — /process-steward/knowledge/open-gaps

data.Purpose: cr-policy-delivery was requested on 2026-07-19 with no DecidedAt. How long has it been sitting, and is that inside what we promised?
data.LayoutHints: Queue by age with the promised decision window marked. Overdue rows are the working list.
data.Name: Stalled Change Requests — /process-steward/governance/stalled-changes

data.Purpose: cr-close-timestamp is Approved, and the model still reads it as OPEN because IsOpen counts Approved as open. Every version it touches reads permanently unfit.
data.LayoutHints: Surface this as a MODEL DEFECT panel, not a data problem: the terminal-state gap, the rows it distorts, and the downstream verdicts it poisons.

AppRouteQuestions.Description: Junction: which RoleQuestions each route helps answer. Deliberately many-to-many — a question is answered across several routes and a route serves several questions. It is not, and should not become, 1:1.

schema.name: AppRouteQuestionId
schema.Description: Stored logical identifier for one AppRouteQuestions row.

schema.name: Name
schema.Description: Human-readable calculated display alias for the AppRouteQuestions row.

schema.name: Route
schema.Description: The route that helps answer the question.

schema.name: Question
schema.Description: The role question this route helps answer.

schema.name: SemanticTypeIri
schema.Description: Semantic type IRI for this row. An extension.

AppRouteReferences.Description: Junction: which other routes a route links to. This is the navigation graph between screens, kept as rows rather than embedded lists so the canonical model stays a DAG.

schema.name: AppRouteReferenceId
schema.Description: Stored logical identifier for one AppRouteReferences row.

schema.name: Name
schema.Description: Human-readable calculated display alias for the AppRouteReferences row.

schema.name: FromRoute
schema.Description: The route that links out.

schema.name: ToRoute
schema.Description: The route being linked to.

schema.name: SemanticTypeIri
schema.Description: Semantic type IRI for this row. An extension.

RulebookTables.Description: Census of every table in this rulebook. The table-level counterpart to RulebookFields, and the anchor every access policy points at. Derived by tools/reconcile_field_catalog.py -- never hand-maintained.

schema.name: RulebookTableId
schema.Description: Primary key: the rulebook table name, verbatim. rulebook-to-postgres synthesizes a lowercased slug PK for a table with no <Entity>Id and rewrites every FK to it, which broke each formula comparing an FK to TableName.

schema.name: TableName
schema.Description: Stored logical identifier: the rulebook table name, e.g. 'Procedures'.

schema.name: Name
schema.Description: Human-readable calculated display alias.

schema.name: PhysicalTable
schema.Description: snake_case Postgres base table name emitted by rulebook-to-postgres.

schema.name: PhysicalView
schema.Description: snake_case Postgres view name (vw_*) carrying the computed columns.

schema.name: SubjectArea
schema.Description: Coarse grouping used to organise role schemas, e.g. 'execution', 'governance'.

schema.name: IsExtension
schema.Description: True when this table is an ERB extension rather than a native/aligned PKO term.

schema.name: FieldCount
schema.Description: Number of catalogued fields on this table.

schema.name: PolicyCount
schema.Description: Number of access policies targeting this table.

schema.name: IsUnsecured
schema.Description: True when RLS is enabled but no policy targets the table, so every principal sees zero rows. A fail-closed table nobody has granted access to.

schema.name: DisagreeingSubstrateCount
schema.Description: How many substrates got at least one cell of this table wrong in the latest conformance run.

schema.name: SemanticTypeIri
schema.Description: Semantic type IRI.

AccessPrincipals.Description: Security principals -- the identities policies attach to. A principal is the console persona a person logs in as; it maps many-to-one onto a domain Role, so 'who may see this row' is expressed once against the domain vocabulary while the UI keeps its own persona names. Each principal owns exactly one Postgres role and one Postgres schema.

schema.name: AccessPrincipalId
schema.Description: Stored logical identifier, e.g. 'principal-controller'.

schema.name: Name
schema.Description: Human-readable calculated display alias.

schema.name: Label
schema.Description: Display label shown in the console role picker.

schema.name: DomainRole
schema.Description: Domain role whose authority this principal exercises.

schema.name: PgRoleName
schema.Description: Postgres role name this principal authenticates as, e.g. 'pko_controller'.

schema.name: SchemaName
schema.Description: Postgres schema that is this principal's entire visible world, e.g. 'pko_controller'.

schema.name: IsAdministrator
schema.Description: True when this principal may read every table and edit access policy.

schema.name: OrganizationScope
schema.Description: Organization inherited from the domain role; the default tenancy boundary for row predicates.

schema.name: RoleLabel
schema.Description: Label of the domain role, for display.

schema.name: PolicyCount
schema.Description: Number of row policies granted to this principal.

schema.name: GrantCount
schema.Description: Number of field grants held by this principal.

schema.name: VisibleTableCount
schema.Description: Number of tables exposed in this principal's schema.

schema.name: HasNoAccess
schema.Description: True when the principal holds no policies at all, so its schema is empty and it can read nothing. Fail-closed by construction.

schema.name: IsOverPrivileged
schema.Description: True when a non-administrator principal can reach every table in the rulebook -- an admin-equivalent principal that was never declared as one.

schema.name: SemanticTypeIri
schema.Description: Semantic type IRI.

AccessPolicies.Description: Row-level security policies: the VERTICAL cut. One row per principal x table x command, carrying the predicate that decides which rows are visible. RowPredicate is emitted verbatim into a Postgres USING clause, so it may call any SECURITY DEFINER calc_* function and therefore reference inference fields many hops down the DAG.

schema.name: AccessPolicyId
schema.Description: Stored logical identifier, e.g. 'pol-controller-procedures-select'.

schema.name: Name
schema.Description: Human-readable calculated display alias.

schema.name: Principal
schema.Description: Principal this policy grants to.

schema.name: TargetTable
schema.Description: Rulebook table this policy guards.

schema.name: Command
schema.Description: SQL command the policy governs: SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE or ALL.

schema.name: RowPredicate
schema.Description: SQL boolean expression emitted into USING(...). Empty means all rows of the table. Must not sub-select the guarded table -- Postgres raises infinite recursion; route such predicates through a SECURITY DEFINER function instead.

schema.name: CheckPredicate
schema.Description: SQL boolean expression emitted into WITH CHECK(...) for write commands. Empty reuses RowPredicate.

schema.name: Rationale
schema.Description: Why this principal is entitled to these rows, in the granting authority's words.

schema.name: ReferencesInference
schema.Description: True when RowPredicate calls a calc_* function, i.e. the cut depends on a derived field rather than a stored column.

schema.name: IsWriteCommand
schema.Description: True when this policy governs a mutating command.

schema.name: IsUnrestricted
schema.Description: True when the policy carries no predicate, exposing every row of the target table to the principal.

schema.name: PrincipalIsAdmin
schema.Description: Whether the granted principal is an administrator.

schema.name: IsUnrestrictedNonAdminGrant
schema.Description: True when a non-administrator principal is granted an unrestricted policy -- a whole-table exposure that no row predicate narrows. The single highest-signal privilege-escalation witness in the model.

schema.name: IsUnwitnessedWrite
schema.Description: True when a write policy has no denial test proving it refuses out-of-scope rows. An untested write grant is an assertion, not evidence.

schema.name: DenialTestCount
schema.Description: Number of denial tests seeded against this policy.

schema.name: SemanticTypeIri
schema.Description: Semantic type IRI.

FieldGrants.Description: Field-level grants: the HORIZONTAL cut. One row per principal x field. A field with no grant row is not filtered from the principal's view -- it is absent from it, so the column does not exist as far as that principal's SQL is concerned.

schema.name: FieldGrantId
schema.Description: Stored logical identifier, e.g. 'fg-controller-Procedures.Title'.

schema.name: Name
schema.Description: Human-readable calculated display alias.

schema.name: Principal
schema.Description: Principal receiving the grant.

schema.name: TargetField
schema.Description: Catalogued field being exposed.

schema.name: CanRead
schema.Description: True when the principal may read this field.

schema.name: CanWrite
schema.Description: True when the principal may write this field.

schema.name: MaskStrategy
schema.Description: How the value is presented when read: 'plain', 'redacted' or 'hashed'.

schema.name: FieldTable
schema.Description: Table the granted field belongs to.

schema.name: FieldName
schema.Description: Name of the granted field.

schema.name: FieldIsDerived
schema.Description: Whether the granted field is a derived (calculated/lookup/aggregation) field.

schema.name: IsWritableDerivedField
schema.Description: True when a derived field has been granted write access. Derived fields are computed by the substrate and cannot be written -- such a grant is incoherent and must be corrected.

schema.name: IsMasked
schema.Description: True when the value is transformed rather than shown verbatim.

schema.name: GrantKeyWhenReadable
schema.Description: Composite echo of principal and table, blank unless readable. Enables single-criterion COUNTIFS rollups of readable columns per principal per table, per the documented multi-criteria COUNTIFS defect.

schema.name: SemanticTypeIri
schema.Description: Semantic type IRI.

RoleSchemas.Description: One Postgres schema per principal -- the principal's entire visible world. The schema is the only entry on that principal's search_path, so a table absent from it cannot be named at all.

schema.name: RoleSchemaId
schema.Description: Stored logical identifier, e.g. 'schema-controller'.

schema.name: Name
schema.Description: Human-readable calculated display alias.

schema.name: Principal
schema.Description: Principal that owns this schema.

schema.name: SchemaName
schema.Description: Postgres schema name, e.g. 'pko_controller'.

schema.name: SearchPath
schema.Description: search_path set for this principal's sessions. The principal's own schema only -- public is deliberately excluded so base tables cannot be named.

schema.name: IsSealed
schema.Description: True when the principal may not create objects in its own schema.

schema.name: ViewCount
schema.Description: Number of views exposed in this schema.

schema.name: IsEmptySchema
schema.Description: True when the schema exposes no views, so the principal can read nothing at all.

schema.name: SemanticTypeIri
schema.Description: Semantic type IRI.

RoleSchemaViews.Description: The emitted views: one per principal x table. ColumnList is DERIVED from FieldGrants, so toggling a single grant changes the emitted DDL with no second edit anywhere. This is what makes an admin's save reshape the database without touching UI code.

schema.name: RoleSchemaViewId
schema.Description: Stored logical identifier, e.g. 'rsv-controller-procedures'.

schema.name: Name
schema.Description: Human-readable calculated display alias.

schema.name: RoleSchema
schema.Description: Schema this view is emitted into.

schema.name: Principal
schema.Description: Principal that will read this view.

schema.name: TargetTable
schema.Description: Rulebook table this view exposes.

schema.name: ViewName
schema.Description: Unqualified view name inside the principal's schema, e.g. 'procedures'.

schema.name: SchemaName
schema.Description: Schema name, from the owning RoleSchemas row.

schema.name: SourceView
schema.Description: Underlying computed view this narrows, e.g. 'vw_procedures'.

schema.name: GrantKey
schema.Description: Composite key matching FieldGrants.GrantKeyWhenReadable, used to roll up this view's readable column count.

schema.name: ColumnCount
schema.Description: Number of columns exposed, derived live from the principal's readable field grants. Change one grant and this view's shape changes.

schema.name: TableFieldCount
schema.Description: Total catalogued fields on the target table.

schema.name: IsFullWidth
schema.Description: True when every field on the table is exposed, so the horizontal cut removes nothing.

schema.name: IsDegenerateView
schema.Description: True when the view exposes zero columns -- an emitted view that cannot be selected from. A generator that emits this has produced invalid DDL.

schema.name: SemanticTypeIri
schema.Description: Semantic type IRI.

JwtClaimMappings.Description: Maps verified JWT claims onto the SQL accessors row predicates call. Magic-links is the notary: it asserts only that the bearer controls an email address. This table records how that verified email, and any additional claims, become values a policy can test.

schema.name: JwtClaimMappingId
schema.Description: Stored logical identifier, e.g. 'claim-email'.

schema.name: Name
schema.Description: Human-readable calculated display alias.

schema.name: ClaimName
schema.Description: Claim key as it appears in the verified JWT payload, e.g. 'email'.

schema.name: SqlAccessor
schema.Description: SQL function a policy calls to read the claim, e.g. 'app.jwt_email()'.

schema.name: IsReservedClaim
schema.Description: True for claims magic-links controls and an app cannot override: email, iss, iat, nbf, exp, sub, tenant_id.

schema.name: MapsToPrincipal
schema.Description: True when this claim is what resolves the caller to an AccessPrincipals row.

schema.name: Description2
schema.Description: What the claim asserts and who vouches for it.

schema.name: UsageCount
schema.Description: Number of policies whose predicate calls this accessor.

schema.name: SemanticTypeIri
schema.Description: Semantic type IRI.

data.Description2: Verified email address. Magic-links asserts only that the bearer controls this mailbox; everything else about the caller is resolved from it inside this database.
data.Name: email -> app.jwt_email()

data.Description2: Magic-links tenant the token was minted for. Pinned so a token from another tenant cannot authenticate here.
data.Name: tenant_id -> app.jwt_tenant_id()

data.Description2: AccessPrincipals row the caller acts as, resolved from the verified email via vw_agents. Not trusted from the token itself.
data.Name: principal -> app.jwt_principal()

data.Description2: Organization the caller belongs to, derived from their principal's domain role. The default tenancy boundary for row predicates.
data.Name: organization -> app.jwt_organization()

AccessDenialTests.Description: Denial witnesses. A policy with no failing case seeded against it is an assertion, not evidence -- the same acceptance bar the rest of this rulebook holds. Each row names a principal, a query, and the row that MUST NOT come back, so a policy that silently stops enforcing is caught by a red test rather than by an incident.

schema.name: AccessDenialTestId
schema.Description: Stored logical identifier, e.g. 'deny-analyst-other-org-procedures'.

schema.name: Name

schema.Description: Why this row must (or must not) be visible, and which predicate it exercises.

schema.Description: True when this test asserts a row the principal IS entitled to. A denial suite with no positive controls cannot distinguish a working policy from one that denies everything.

schema.Description: Distinct process variants discovered in the mined event log.

ConformanceSubstrates.Description: Every tool that compiles this rulebook into something that computes. One is the answer-key author (compile-rulebook bakes derived values into the rulebook's own rows); the rest are graded substrates that re-derive those values natively and are scored cell by cell against them.

schema.name: ConformanceSubstrateId
schema.Description: Substrate name as the conformance harness knows it, e.g. 'effortless-python'.

schema.name: Name
schema.Description: Human-readable calculated display alias.

schema.name: Label
schema.Description: Short human label, e.g. 'Python'.

schema.name: Transpiler
schema.Description: The effortless.json tool that produces this substrate, e.g. 'rulebook-to-python'.

schema.name: OutputFolder
schema.Description: Project folder the tool writes into, e.g. '/effortless-python'.

schema.name: Engine
schema.Description: What actually evaluates the formulas: a database, a language runtime, a spreadsheet engine or a reasoner.

schema.name: HowItComputes
schema.Description: One paragraph a curious reader can follow: what the tool emits and how the harness makes it produce answers.

schema.name: Role
schema.Description: 'answer-key' for the tool whose stored values every other substrate is graded against; 'graded' for everything else.

schema.name: SortOrder
schema.Description: Display order.

schema.name: IsGraded
schema.Description: True for substrates the harness scores.

schema.name: RunCount
schema.Description: How many recorded conformance runs graded this substrate.

schema.name: LatestCellsTested
schema.Description: Cells graded in the latest run: every (record x derived field) pair in the answer keys.

schema.name: LatestCellsPassed
schema.Description: Cells this substrate computed identically to the answer key in the latest run.

schema.name: LatestHarnessErrors
schema.Description: 1 when the latest run could not execute this substrate at all.

schema.name: LatestCellsFailed
schema.Description: Cells this substrate got wrong, or did not produce, in the latest run.

schema.name: LatestScore
schema.Description: Percent of cells agreeing with the answer key in the latest run.

schema.name: DisagreeingFieldCount
schema.Description: Derived fields on which this substrate got at least one cell wrong in the latest run.

schema.name: DisagreeingTableCount
schema.Description: Tables on which this substrate got at least one cell wrong in the latest run.

schema.name: IsFullyConformant
schema.Description: True when the latest run graded this substrate, it ran, and every cell agreed. A substrate never graded is not conformant.

schema.name: SemanticTypeIri
schema.Description: Semantic type IRI.

data.Label: compile-rulebook
data.HowItComputes: Runs first in the build and rewrites the rulebook in place: every calculated, lookup and aggregation value is computed across all tables to a fixed point and upserted into the rows. Those stored values become the answer keys. It is not graded against itself; when another substrate disagrees, either side can be the one that is wrong.
data.Name: compile-rulebook

data.Label: PostgreSQL
data.Engine: PostgreSQL views and calc_* SQL functions
data.HowItComputes: rulebook-to-postgres emits a table, a set of calc_* functions and a vw_<entity> view per table. The database is reset from the rulebook, and the harness reads SELECT * from every view.
data.Name: PostgreSQL

data.Label: Python
data.HowItComputes: rulebook-to-python emits an SDK with one computed property per derived field. The harness loads the blank test rows (raw fields only) and asks the SDK for every derived value.
data.Name: Python

data.Label: Go
data.HowItComputes: rulebook-to-go emits a Go module. The harness compiles it with go build, runs it over the blank test rows, and reads back every derived value.
data.Name: Go

data.Label: TypeScript
data.HowItComputes: rulebook-to-typescript emits a typed SDK. The harness compiles it with tsc and runs it on Node over the blank test rows.
data.Name: TypeScript

data.Label: C# / Entity Framework
data.HowItComputes: rulebook-to-entity-framework emits C# data classes whose Formula* properties compute derived fields. The harness compiles them with EF Core into a runner, loads the blank test rows into the generated context over a throwaway SQLite database, and reads every computed property back per row.
data.Name: C# / Entity Framework

data.Label: Excel
data.Engine: Spreadsheet formulas (cached values read with openpyxl)
data.HowItComputes: rulebook-to-xlsx compiles every formula into a real Excel formula over cells in the same workbook. The harness reads the workbook's cached values, after a LibreOffice recalc when LibreOffice is installed; a value that was never calculated reads as blank.
data.Name: Excel

data.Label: OWL / SHACL
data.HowItComputes: rulebook-to-owl emits an ontology, an ABox of individuals carrying raw fields only, and one SHACL-AF SPARQL rule per derived field. The harness executes the rules in dependency order and reads the inferred triples back.
data.Name: OWL / SHACL
